properties.Name: Omarama Saddle
properties.Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock, peneplain offset of several hundred metres. Definite fault scarp at N end of fault, and likely ones at far south end of fault. Barrell 2019 proposes 0.2 mm/yr SR, adopted here as pref. Nominal SR min/max

properties.Name: Rocks Creek
properties.References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207); Beanland and Fellows 1985
properties.Comments: Array of east-facing Quaternary fault scarps/monoclines, inferred association W-dipping bedrock fault. Interpred as a back-fault off Omaranma Saddle Fault; Barrell 2019 assigned SR as not independently rupturing structure.

properties.Name: Hawkdun
properties.References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
properties.Comments: Major fault in bedrock, up to 1 km Late Cenozoic peneplain offset. Blue Lake SR is applied to the Hawkdun Fault. No recognised Quaternary scarps, though in the mountain-front setting, conceivable no long-term recognisable surface evidence persists

properties.Name: Black Hill
properties.References: Barrell and Van Dissen 2003 (CR2003/107); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
properties.Comments: Major fault in bedrock, with as much as ~500 m offset of the peneplain, up to the southeast. Proposed as possible active fault by Barrell 2016. No definitive evidence for Late Quaternary movement, and nominal slip rates inferred.

properties.Name: Waitaki
properties.References: Barrell and Van Dissen 2003 (CR2003/107); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
properties.Comments: Major fault in bedrock, with as much as ~1200 m uplift of the peneplain to the southwest. There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation, nominal slip rates inferred.

properties.Name: Waimate
properties.References: Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166) and references therein
properties.Comments: Up up to 1 km Late Cenozoic throw.  Hunters Fault dips and rakes applied. Nominal slow SRs aplied. Lack of known deformation on relatively old fans and terraces is basis for slow SRs and QC of 4 in 100 ky timeframe

properties.Name: Awamoa
properties.Comments: Marine terrace height change (~7 m) is the main evidence for activity. Due to N-S strike, it is assessed as pure dip slip, and assigned a preferred slip rate of 0.1 mm/yr (9 m vertical offset since ~125 ka, resolved onto a 45 degree fault plane.

properties.Name: Gibson

properties.Name: Falstone

properties.Name: Ostler South

properties.References: Cox and Barrell 2007 (Aoraki QMAP);  Barrell 2013 (CR2012/325); this compilation
properties.Comments: Prominent fault block, up to 0.5 km throw on peneplain; correlated with Quaternary faults at Rakiaia Gorge. Best SR based on ~30 m throw on ~165 ka lake sediments, resolved onto 60 deg pure reverse fault (sense inferred from strike).

properties.Name: Redcliffe
properties.References: Cox and Barrell 2007 (Aoraki QMAP);  Barrell 2009 (CR2009/227); Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Suspected but not confirmed post-glacial scarps; SR pref based on 2.5 m scarp on ~18 ka surface, max is value given by Barrell 2009. Assumed pure reverse, dips from CFM retained. Revised version of part of Double Hill Fault of CFM

properties.Name: Edith
properties.References: Cox and Barrell 2007 (Aoraki QMAP);  this compilation
properties.Comments: Basement rock with well-defined peneplain surface uplifted ~200 m to the west against peneplain remnants.  No known Quat offsets, nominal slip rate applied.

properties.Name: Catherine
properties.References: Cox and Barrell 2007 (Aoraki QMAP);  this compilation
properties.Comments: Basement rock uplifted hundreds of metres to the west against Tertiary outlier and extrensive peneplain dip slope. New name to avoid confusion with active Blue Mountain Fault in South Otago. No known Quat offsets, nominal slip rate applied.

properties.Name: Rapuwai
properties.References: Wellman 1953; Cox and Barrell 2007 (Aoraki QMAP);  Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Prominent fault block, basement exposed in centre, hundreds of metres of Late Cenozoic uplift. No known Quat offsets, but mid-late Q uplift can be inferred NE of Geraldine. Slow SR, slightly above nominal, inferred.

properties.Name: Grampian
properties.References: Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Major ~N-striking fault in bedrock, that has uplifted the Grampian Mountains that separate Hakatarmea valley from Mackenzie basin, with peneplain offset of as much as ~1000 m. No evidence for LQ offset, nominal slip rates assigned.

properties.Name: Mt Sutton
properties.References: Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Major ~N-striking fault in bedrock, with uplift of unnamed range (highest point, Mt Sutton) northeast of the Aviemore basin.  There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation, although rugged hill terrain reduces likelihood of its preservation.

properties.Name: Campbell Hills
properties.References: Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Peneplain offset of typically ~500 m. There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation, although rugged hill terrain reduces likelihood of its preservation. Nominal slip rates inferred.

properties.Name: Waikaia
properties.References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Represents an en-cechelon array of fault slices, that uplift basement to the E against Tertiary strata by many hundreds of metres. No reported evidence for Late Q deformation, nominal slip rates applied.

properties.Name: Wendon Valley
properties.References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: This source is sub-parallel to the Waikaia source. Name is from QMAP, throw has uplifted the Black Umbrella Range, by hundreds of metres relative to Tertiary outliers. No reported evidence for Late Q deformation, nominal slip rates applied.

properties.Name: Mid Dome
properties.References: Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Inferred to account for prominent elevation of the Mid Dome ridge, up to ~1 km throw on peneplain.  Nominal slip rates, mod-steep east dip, and some movement obliquity inferred.

properties.Name: Acton
properties.References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Connects Late Q scarps on Five Rivers Plain and fault scarp up Acton Stream, shown on QMAP. Approx 2 m scarp on ~18 ka surface basis for slip rates, plus topographic expression (up to E) in hill country.

properties.Name: White Hill
properties.References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
properties.Comments: Uplifts Murihiku basement against Tertiary inlier, and acconts for uplift of Taringatura Hills (several hundred metres of relief). QMAP shows locally preseved Late Q scarp.

properties.Name: Hedgehope
properties.References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); this compilation
properties.Comments: Uplifts the Hokonui Hills and represents that strucural margin fault zone that controls the famed 'Gore' structural gap across the Southland Syncline in basement rock. No reported Late Q activity, nominal slip rates applied.

properties.Name: McKerchar
properties.References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Carter and Norris 2005 (SR2004/23); Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
properties.Comments: Referred to by Cater and Norris as 'Takitimu Boundary Fault Zone'; complex fault zone. Remanent Quat scarps. Accounts for main uplift of Takitimu Mountains. Fault dips and rake is guess. Scarps on old fans give slip rate estimates (see Barrell 2019)
